title: Cap. II: Scholastici — causes of election (moral works / use of grace); Rom. 9 overthrows
pass_a_gloss: But let us descend from the Semipelagians unto the Scholastics. Out of these not a few teach that a cause is given of predestination or election, insofar as it falls upon this man rather than upon that. And here certain ones put forward good moral works which precede the grace of justification; others, good works which follow; others the foresight good use of Divine grace. But it is hardly necessary that I should linger in refuting these opinions, which all are overthrown by that one stroke of the Apostle, Rom. ix. 11. The children being not yet born, when they had done nothing good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth, it was said, &c. Key lemmas: Scholastici; causa praedestinationis/electionis; opera bona moralia ante/post justificationem; praevisus bonus usus gratiae; Rom. ix. 11 non ex operibus.
pass_b_english: Next, down from the Semipelagians to the Scholastics. Not a few of them teach that predestination — or election — has a cause insofar as it falls on this man rather than that. Some plead good moral works before justifying grace; others good works after it; others foresight of a good use of God's grace. I need not linger refuting these views: one blow from the Apostle flattens them all (Rom. 9:11) — the children not yet born, having done nothing good or evil, so that God's purpose according to election might stand, not from works but from the One who calls.
source_text: Sed descendamus a Semipelagianis ad Scholasticos. Ex hisce nonnulli docent causam dari praedestinationis seu electionis, quatenus cadit super hunc hominem potius quam super illum. Atque hic quidam obtendunt opera bona moralia, quae antecedunt gratiam justificationis; alii, opera bona quae subsequuntur; alii praevisum bonum usum gratiae Divinae. Verum haud necesse est ut in hisce sententiis refellendis inhaeream, quae omnes unico illo Apostoli ictu prosternuntur Rom. ix. 11. Nondum natis pueris, cum nihil fecissent boni vel mali, ut propositum Dei secundum electionem maneret, non ex operibus, sed ex vocante, dictum est, &c.
